# Decisions

Closed questions. Each names the date it closed.

## Generated dependency files are never committed

Every file forge-factory writes is added to the owning repo's gitignore.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** A version committed in a repo is a version written twice, and bumping it then costs a pull request per repo.

## A repo is never cloned and built alone

Work happens in a synced workspace. forge-factory is the only repo that must build from a lone checkout.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** Generated dependency files cannot exist if a lone clone has to work, and forge-factory is what materialises them.

## Manifests are generated whole, not in marked blocks

package.json and pyproject.toml are written in full. No npm scripts.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** A marked block invites hand edits beside it. Scripts would duplicate forge stages, which is a second way to run the same thing. Every golden-typescript stage already calls pnpm exec directly, so dropping scripts cost nothing.

## A repo carries its own tool config, verbatim

toolConfig in a repo's forge.yaml factory block is appended to the generated manifest unchanged.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** The first generated pyproject.toml deleted pytest options, ruff rules and coverage omits. Generating whole files only works if everything those files hold has somewhere to live, and tool settings belong to the repo, not to the workspace.

## forge-factory and forge-ci share a contract, not a dependency

Both speak the transport in forge-revision-spec. Neither imports the other.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** Either tool has to work alone, and swapping the state engine has to move both without a release of either.

## Branch based compositions are dropped

Members are worked on from main. forge-cu is archived.

**Decided 2026-08-19.** A second repo carrying its own branch state, for one person, is overhead with no reader.
